headline: Intel confirmed in talks with AUO for Micro LED glass-substrate advanced packaging targeting CPO — INTC pops in pre-market
summary: Digitimes reports Intel and AU Optronics are collaborating on Micro LED substrate-based advanced packaging for co-packaged optics (CPO) and high-density AI compute, embedding Micro LEDs into glass substrates via through-glass vias. Intel shares rallied roughly 5-6% pre-market on the report, positioning the foundry business as a differentiated packaging player alongside its TSMC/NVIDIA tie-ups.

headline: Xi Jinping state visit to Washington confirmed for Sept 23-25; chip export controls and AI on the agenda
summary: Beijing confirmed Xi Jinping's first US state visit since 2015. Trump is hosting a state dinner on Sept 24 with Sam Altman, Jensen Huang and Tim Cook attending, putting semiconductor licensing and AI diplomacy front-and-centre. Chinese customs is still blocking H200 shipments Washington previously licensed; markets are treating the visit as a potential catalyst for either a tariff/export-control thaw or escalation.

headline: House passes Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3, forcing datacenter loads >100 MW to bear their own grid costs
summary: Sponsored by Reps. Castor (D-FL) and Evans (R-CO), the bill requires states to consider standards preventing large computational loads from shifting generation and transmission costs onto residential ratepayers. The 417-3 tally is the most lopsided AI-related vote in congressional history; only Reps. Lee, Ramirez and Tlaib opposed. The Senate has not yet acted. Structural tailwind for behind-the-meter power (Bloom, fuel cells, on-site SMR) and modest headwind for hyperscalers absorbing more of the interconnection tab.

headline: Nuclear stocks give back Ratepayer-Act rally on Friday — NuScale -7%, Oklo -5%, Centrus -3%
summary: Friday's session saw SMR developers unwind Thursday's post-vote enthusiasm. NuScale (SMR) fell 7% to close a difficult week, Oklo -5% to $37.57, Centrus (LEU) -3%. Oklo is now down 45% YTD and NuScale -36% YTD. Analysts framed Thursday's spike as tactical positioning rather than a durable rerating.

headline: CoreWeave prices $3B convertibles plus 35M-share ATM as $3.6T AI-financing scrutiny intensifies
summary: CoreWeave (CRWV) launched a $3B convertible notes offering due 2033 with a $500M greenshoe, alongside an up-to-35M-share at-the-market equity program. Shares fell >4% Thursday. New research mapping $3.6T of AI infrastructure exposure singles out CRWV and Oracle as the most leveraged names in the supply chain, raising concerns about how the buildout gets financed if hyperscaler capex outpaces cash flow.

headline: GE Vernova CEO says $200B backlog milestone likely to be hit early in 2027 on Q3 order strength
summary: At the Morgan Stanley Laguna conference, CEO Scott Strazik said GEV exited Q2 at $176B backlog and Q3 order momentum has him confident the $200B mark comes 'very early in 2027' — ahead of schedule. Read-through supports the electrification bid: Eaton (ETN) +2% and Quanta Services +2% on the day. Reinforces the House Rating thesis on grid and turbine tightness through 2027.

headline: Bloom Energy stacks $25B in datacenter backlog and financing as fuel cells win the on-site-power bid; Plug stays on the sidelines
summary: Bloom (BE) and Brookfield have expanded their AI-infrastructure JV from $5B to $25B, funding on-site fuel-cell projects that let hyperscalers bypass interconnection queues. Bloom has already booked $7.65B of datacenter-linked contracts in early 2026. Plug Power's CEO reiterated Q2 that the company is not chasing the datacenter opportunity, staying focused on material handling, electrolyzers and green hydrogen, though a July 2026 Microsoft PEM-fuel-cell backup pilot remains active.

headline: AI server rotation lifts HPE +9%, SMCI +6%, DELL +3% as memory tightness and OEM allocation gains broaden the hardware bid
summary: Thursday's session saw a targeted hardware rotation with HPE +9%, Super Micro +6%, Dell +3% on rising memory prices and OEM share gains as Supermicro's export-control overhang leaves NVIDIA GPU allocation available for DELL and HPE Vera Rubin platforms unveiled at GTC 2026. Higher DRAM/HBM ASPs are a net positive to server revenue but a squeeze on Supermicro's thin margins.

headline: Fed hiked 25 bps to 3.75-4.00% Wednesday — first hike since 2023; tech shrugged it off with Nasdaq +1.6% Thursday
summary: The FOMC delivered a unanimous 25 bps hike, its first tightening in three years, citing sticky inflation, resilient labor and rising oil. Nasdaq gained 1.59% Thursday and futures are up ~1.1% pre-open Monday as oil retreats and mega-cap tech cash flow absorbs the higher discount rate. Watch the 2027 dot plot — a further hike would pressure highly-levered names (CRWV, ORCL) more than the mega-caps.

headline: Nasdaq futures +1.1% pre-open Monday as chipmakers rally into US-China talks and Intel-AUO packaging news
summary: Dow futures +401 pts (+0.77%), S&P 500 futures +54.25 (+0.70%), Nasdaq futures +334.50 (+1.12%) heading into Monday's open. Oil retreated and chipmakers led the pre-bell bid, with Intel up ~5-6% on the AUO Micro LED CPO partnership scoop from Digitimes. Traders positioning ahead of Xi Jinping's state visit later in the week.
